Camila / team — thanks for the heads up and the packet. High level guidance below; see accounting notes at the end.

Short answer: we can support either path, but preference depends on timing and audit trail needs.

Option A — Invoice offset (preferred if buyer wants immediate cashflow relief):
- We prepare an Accounts Receivable adjustment to net INV-2197 against a promotional allowance. This is effectively an offset journal that reduces the open invoice balance and posts to promo expense / contra-revenue GL.
- Pros: faster posting (can be done in current AR cycle), avoids creating a separate customer credit memo line that might complicate collections.
- Cons: needs clear approval record (email + PO or written acceptance) attached to AR transaction for audit.

Option B — Standard credit memo (preferred for audit clarity):
- Issue a formal credit memo (RM-8342) referencing INV-2197, post credit memo on Dec 31 (or Jan 1 if they insist).
- Pros: clean trail in ERP, easier to reconcile for quarter close.
- Cons: may post slightly later than an AR adjustment and could affect their cashflow timing.

Accounting asks before we proceed:
1) Confirm legal entity (Onward Health — US entity?)
2) Confirm currency (USD stated) and tax treatment (no VAT here)
3) Provide formal acceptance (email approval acceptable; PO or signed addendum preferred)
4) For Option A we need GL-mapping confirmation; attach the completed GL-mapping file (I attached a template: GL-mapping-accounting.xlsx)

If you want us to move fast for month-end cashflow relief, say "GO OPTION A" and attach the acceptance; we'll schedule AR adj this week. If they prefer the formal route for audit, say "GO OPTION B" and we will draft RM-8342 and aim to post on Dec 31.

—Marcus
